sources.title: Pieter Naaijkens, Quantum Spin Systems on Infinite Lattices, extended and corrected Summer 2016 lecture notes, arXiv:1311.2717v2
sources.locator: Complete 157-page author-hosted PDF. Read the full relevant ranges: §3.1, printed pp. 50–53 (PDF pp. 51–53), including the finite-excitation spin-chain basis, local action, irreducibility argument, and polarization comparison; §3.4, printed pp. 74–77 (PDF pp. 74–77), including Definition 3.4.4, the finite Gibbs/KMS calculation and uniqueness discussion, and the adjacent general KMS-limit results.

contents.name: §3.1, finite-excitation basis, local spin-flip action, printed pp. 50–53
contents.support: The notes construct the spin-1/2, one-dimensional finite-flip basis. The assigned definition gives the full q-dimensional Z^d configuration construction and its norm-continuous extension.

contents.name: §3.1, irreducibility of the finite-excitation representation, printed pp. 52–53
contents.support: Naaijkens proves the spin-chain case by cyclic vectors; the assigned lemma supplies the complete local matrix-unit commutant proof for finite q and d≥1.

contents.name: §3.4, Definition 3.4.4, physical-time KMS strip and reversed upper edge, printed p. 74
contents.support: The assigned theorem uses the same closed strip boundary order through the exact earlier KMS-definition supplier and preserves width beta*hbar.

contents.name: §3.4, finite Gibbs/KMS calculation and finite-volume uniqueness, printed pp. 76–77
contents.support: This is the finite-matrix input used in the onsite product theorem; the local proof supplies the exact uniqueness argument and carries the physical-time convention.

contents.name: §3.4, Theorem 3.4.6, derivation/logarithmic inequality characterization, printed p. 75
contents.reason: The assigned proof works directly with bounded closed-strip functions at fixed beta and does not assert or use the generator-domain logarithmic inequality characterization.

contents.name: §3.4, Proposition 3.4.7, limits with varying dynamics or inverse temperatures, printed pp. 75–76
contents.reason: The assigned result fixes one onsite interaction and one positive beta; the broader varying-dynamics and zero-temperature limit theorem is not used or claimed.

sources.title: David Ruelle, Topics in Quantum Statistical Mechanics and Operator Algebras, complete author-hosted lecture notes, arXiv:math-ph/0107009v1

contents.name: Chapter 2 §1, local spin matrix algebras and quasi-local completion, printed pp. 17–18
contents.support: The representation is defined on the exact quasi-local completion, with local factor inclusions and no global tensor-product identification.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §5, commutant and irreducibility criterion, printed pp. 42–44
contents.support: The assigned lemma states irreducibility as a scalar commutant and proves that interface directly using local projections and matrix units.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, closed-strip KMS condition, printed pp. 13–14
contents.support: The assigned proof uses the bounded physical-time strip and matching lower/upper correlation ordering.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §6, finite Gibbs state and its KMS identity/uniqueness, printed pp. 24–25
contents.support: The finite onsite Gibbs calculation supports the finite-region uniqueness step; the infinite product conclusion is proved locally and conditionally.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §5, normal states and trace-class density characterization, printed p. 10
contents.reason: The assigned definition uses order-continuity under bounded increasing positive nets and the theorem proves the trace-class case directly; no equivalence of normality conventions is assumed.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §6, general infinite-volume Gibbs/KMS equivalence, printed p. 25
contents.reason: The pair treats only the explicitly defined onsite product model and does not use or assert the broader Gibbs/KMS equivalence for arbitrary interactions.
